start.text: *1:04 a.m. Her phone lights up the ceiling. Ploy.*

call_2.speaker: Ploy
call_2.text: "He left me on read, Elysia. For three hours. And then he sent a meme."

call_3.text: *Elysia lies in the dark with the phone on the pillow next to her ear. Her eyes are closed.*

call_4.speaker: Elysia
call_4.text: History presentation tomorrow. No, today. And it's Monday. Kay always gets pad kra pao on Mondays.

call_6.text: *She says it because it is, and because Ploy needs her to.*

call_7.speaker: Ploy
call_7.text: "Right?? Okay, so here's what he said, I'll read you the whole thing—"

choices.text: "Ploy, I'm so sorry, I have to sleep. Tomorrow at lunch?"

call_stay_1.text: *She stays on until 3:07 a.m. Ploy feels better by the end. Elysia can hear it.*

call_stay_2.speaker: Elysia
call_stay_2.text: Good. That's good. That's what I'm for.

call_sleep_2.speaker: Ploy
call_sleep_2.text: "...Oh. Yeah. Sure. Sorry for bothering you."

call_sleep_3.speaker: Elysia
call_sleep_3.real_text: "You're not bothering me, I'm just so tired—"

call_sleep_5.text: *Click. Elysia lies awake until two anyway, replaying "sorry for bothering you" until it stops sounding like words.*

bfast_1.text: *At breakfast, Pun is eating eggs with one hand and holding a jar with the other.*

bfast_2.speaker: Pun
bfast_2.text: "Look. LOOK. I found him by the drain."

bfast_3.text: *Inside the jar is a twig with something bright yellow spread across it. Like spilled egg yolk, branching into veins like a tiny map.*

bfast_4.text: *Elysia knows exactly what it is. She knows the Latin name. She knows it isn't mold at all. Not a plant. Not an animal.*

bfast_5.text: *In third grade she'd have been on the floor next to Pun, nose against the glass.*

choices.text: "That's a slime mold! It's not even mold, it's—"

bfast_just_1.text: *Pun's face falls, just a little. He puts the jar next to his plate and eats his eggs.*

bfast_just_2.text: *Elysia doesn't look at the jar again. It's hard.*

bfast_rhino_1.text: *It comes out before she can check.*

bfast_rhino_3.speaker: Elysia
bfast_rhino_3.text: "I just... read about it once. Eat your eggs. You'll be late."

bfast_rhino_4.text: *But Pun keeps looking at her all through breakfast like she's a wizard.*

gate_1.text: *At the gate, Ploy has her arm linked through Elysia's and is telling Jane and Bow about the meme. Elysia laughs at all the right places.*

gate_2.text: *Then she feels it, the way she always does. Kay is somewhere behind her.*

gate_3.text: *She turns around. There he is, by the gate. Very still, looking at her like she's far away.*

gate_4.speaker: Elysia
gate_4.text: He looks so tired. Grey. Did he sleep at all?

gate_5.text: *She smiles and waves. Kay waves back a second too late, a little too stiff. Like a robot remembering how arms work.*

gate_7.speaker: Elysia
gate_7.text: No. He's just Kay. He's always like that at school.

gate_9.speaker: Ploy
gate_9.text: "Elysia, focus, I'm getting to the part with the meme."

gate_10.text: *She mouths "later!" to Kay and lets herself get pulled away.*

line_1.text: *Lunch. She planned it. She'll admit that to herself, though never to anyone else.*

line_2.text: *She gets in the pad kra pao line right behind Kay and waits for him to notice. He doesn't. He's staring at the menu board like it's homework.*

line_4.text: *He turns around so fast he nearly drops his tray.*

line_5.speaker: Elysia
line_5.text: "Pad kra pao again? You're so predictable."

line_6.speaker: Kay
line_6.text: "Y-you're one to talk. You're in the same line."

line_7.speaker: Elysia
line_7.text: "Mm. And why do you think I'm in this line?"

line_8.text: *She watches him think about it. She can see him get there, and then back away from it, the way he backs away from everything.*

line_13.speaker: Elysia
line_13.text: "You know, I always have to come find you. You never come find me."

line_14.speaker: Kay
line_14.text: "I didn't want to bother you. You're always with your friends."

line_15.speaker: Elysia
line_15.text: "Always with your friends." Why does that sound like "always somewhere I'm not allowed"?

line_17.speaker: Lunch Lady
line_17.text: "Are you two ordering, or just flirting?"

line_18.text: *She laughs. Kay goes red to his ears.*

line_19.speaker: Elysia
line_19.text: "Come sit with us if you want, okay?"

line_20.text: *She carries her tray back to the table by the window, glancing over her shoulder once.*

line_21.text: *Check: Ploy, eyebrows up. Jane, grinning. Bow, phone.*

line_23.speaker: Kay
line_23.text: "Hey. Is it okay if I sit here?"

line_25.text: *The table goes silent. Ploy looks at Kay. Then at Elysia. Then at Kay again.*

line_27.speaker: Elysia
line_27.text: "Hey. Stop staring at him. Eat your food."

line_28.text: *Her face is hot. She's pouting, but not because she's upset. She's so happy she could scream.*

line_29.speaker: Elysia
line_29.text: He came over. He actually came over. In front of everyone.

line_30.text: *Under the table, she bumps his foot with hers. Just once.*

line_31.text: *When Kay leaves to return his tray, Ploy leans in.*

line_32.speaker: Ploy
line_32.text: "So that's the boyfriend. He's cute. He's just... so quiet. Kind of weird?"

line_33.text: *"Weird" lands somewhere old in her chest. The third-grade place.*

line_34.text: *Check: Ploy, smiling, not mean. Jane, nodding. Bow, waiting for my answer.*

shy_3.text: *Everybody nods. The moment passes, smooth as water.*

shy_4.text: *Under the smile, a small voice says you should have said something. She smiles over it until it's quiet.*

notweird_1.text: *It comes out sharper than she meant. Ploy's eyebrows go up.*

notweird_2.speaker: Ploy
notweird_2.text: "Okay, defensive. I didn't mean it bad."

notweird_3.speaker: Elysia
notweird_3.text: "I know! I know. Sorry. He's just quiet. That's all."
notweird_3.real_text: "No, I meant it. He's not weird."

notweird_4.text: *Ploy changes the subject. Elysia's heart is still beating too fast ten minutes later.*

walk_1.text: *After school. Kay is halfway through the gate.*

walk_2.speaker: Elysia
walk_2.text: Do it. You're allowed to walk home with your own boyfriend.

walk_4.text: *Loud and bright, so it sounds easy. Behind her, Ploy whispers something to Jane. Elysia doesn't hear what. She hears the whisper.*

walk_5.text: *Kay looks at her. Then past her, at her friends. His face does something careful.*

walk_6.speaker: Kay
walk_6.text: "I... shouldn't. You don't want people looking at us like that."

walk_7.text: *For half a second, something in her face drops. Like missing a step.*

walk_12.text: *She walks off alone. The smile stays on past the 7-Eleven, the bus stop, the corner. A beat too long. Then a hundred.*

walk_13.speaker: Elysia
walk_13.text: "You don't want people looking at us like that." Like what?

walk_14.speaker: Elysia
walk_14.text: Like the slime girl and the boy who has to stand next to her.

walk_15.text: *She knows it isn't fair. Kay is the gentlest person she knows.*

walk_16.speaker: Elysia
walk_16.text: But he came to the table. And the second my friends were watching, he said no.

walk_17.speaker: Elysia
walk_17.text: He's embarrassed of me. Like everyone. Like third grade.

walk_18.text: *6:30. Mint calls. Mint has called on Mondays since they were six.*

walk_19.speaker: Mint
walk_19.text: "So? Did you get him in the pad kra pao line?"

walk_20.speaker: Elysia
walk_20.text: "I did! He sat with us. And then after school I asked him to walk home, and he said..."

walk_21.text: *She's on her bed, looking at the ceiling.*

walk_22.speaker: Elysia
walk_22.text: "He said he shouldn't. Because people would look at us."

mint_hurt_1.speaker: Elysia
mint_hurt_1.text: "It kind of hurt. Like he doesn't want people to know he's with me."

mint_hurt_2.speaker: Mint
mint_hurt_2.text: "Do you want me to fight him?"

mint_hurt_8.text: *It's what Mint says when she's already decided something. Elysia doesn't ask what. She should have.*

mint_fine_1.speaker: Elysia
mint_fine_1.text: "It's fine! He's just busy. He's always busy."

mint_fine_4.text: *Mint sighs the sigh of someone who has known you for eleven years and is choosing not to fight about it tonight.*

tue_1.text: *Tuesday. 6:20 a.m. She's been awake since five, typing.*

tue_2.text: *"why didn't you want to walk with me." Delete.*

tue_4.text: *"are you embarrassed of me." Delete. Delete. Delete.*

choices.text: "can i ask why you didn't want to walk yesterday?"

tue_cheer_1.speaker: Elysia
tue_cheer_1.text: goooood morning!! ☀️ did u eat breakfast

tue_cheer_2.text: *Like yesterday never happened. She's very good at that.*

tue_cheer_5.text: *She sends the sticker of the furious cat.*

tue_cheer_7.speaker: Elysia
tue_cheer_7.text: He's fine. We're fine. Everything's normal.

tue_cheer_8.text: *She doesn't believe it. She puts the phone in her bag anyway.*

tue_ask_1.text: *She sends it before the version can stop her, and throws the phone onto the bed like it's hot.*

tue_ask_3.speaker: Kay
tue_ask_3.text: sorry about yesterday. i didn't mean it like that.

tue_ask_4.speaker: Elysia
tue_ask_4.text: Like what? What did you mean?

tue_ask_6.text: *She looks at it. Then, before she can stop herself:*

tue_ask_8.text: *The typing dots appear and vanish three times.*

tue_ask_10.text: *He didn't explain. But he said sorry, and he didn't say "it's fine." She holds onto that.*

garden_1.text: *The second week, Ploy plans a mall trip for Wednesday.*

garden_3.speaker: Elysia
garden_3.text: "I can't, I have to help my brother with a thing."

garden_4.text: *It's a lie. She's never lied to Ploy about plans before. But Kay has been at the school garden every afternoon. She's seen him from the art room window. Alone, holding the hose.*

garden_5.text: *Four beds behind the science building. Tiny seedlings. Very, very wet soil.*

garden_6.text: *Kay looks up and sees her. For a second his face is unguarded. Surprised. Happy?*

garden_10.speaker: Kay
garden_10.text: "You were in the area. Behind the science building."

garden_12.text: *She crouches by the chili bed so he can't see her face. And then she sees it.*

garden_13.text: *On the old log edging the bed, where the soil is wettest: something bright yellow, spread across the bark. Like spilled egg yolk, branching into veins like a tiny map.*

garden_15.speaker: Elysia
garden_15.text: "Oh. Oh! Kay. Come here. Don't move fast."

garden_16.speaker: Elysia
garden_16.text: "That's a slime mold. Physarum, I think. It's not a mold, it's not a plant, it's not an animal, it doesn't even have a brain, and it can still solve a maze. Scientists put oat flakes down in the shape of the cities around Tokyo, and it grew a network that looked almost exactly like the real train lines—"

garden_18.text: *She stops in the middle of the sentence and glances over her shoulder at the path.*

garden_20.speaker: Elysia
garden_20.text: "Sorry. That's weird. Nobody cares about slime."

garden_21.text: *Kay is looking at her. Not at the slime mold. At her.*

garden_24.text: *Check: his face. Not polite. Not pity. It's...*

garden_25.text: *She doesn't have a word for it. Nobody but Mint has ever looked at her like that while she was being slime girl.*

garden_maze.speaker: Elysia
garden_maze.text: "Okay. Watch. You put food down, and it finds it. Every single time."

garden_go_1.text: *Slowly at first, testing the ice. Then faster, because he keeps nodding and asking questions. How does it know where to go without a brain? Can it hurt you?*

garden_go_2.text: *Pink slime molds. Slime molds that crawl a few centimeters an hour. The one she kept in her lunchbox in third grade that found its way out of a paper maze overnight.*

garden_go_3.text: *For twenty minutes she doesn't check anyone's face once.*

garden_go_3b.text: *She checks the path twice. Nobody's there. Both times, Kay waits for her to come back.*

garden_go_4.text: *When she runs out of words, the sun is lower, and Kay is smiling at her.*

garden_stop_1.speaker: Elysia
garden_stop_1.text: "Haha, anyway— wow, your chilies are so small! Is that normal?"

garden_stop_2.text: *Kay looks at her for a second like he's trying to work something out.*

garden_stop_4.text: *She doesn't look at the log again.*

garden_gate_1.text: *They walk to the gate. In the evening light, she looks at him properly for the first time in days.*

garden_gate_2.speaker: Elysia
garden_gate_2.text: Grey. He's grey, like a photo left in the sun.

garden_gate_6.text: *He laughs it off. She doesn't laugh.*

garden_gate_7.speaker: Elysia
garden_gate_7.text: He's carrying something. He's always carrying something.

garden_gate_8.speaker: Elysia
garden_gate_8.text: He'll tell me when he's ready.

nam_1.text: *The third week. In art class, Nam's plush frog keychain falls off her bag and skids across the floor to Ploy's feet.*

nam_2.speaker: Ploy
nam_2.text: "Oh my god. Who brings a plushie to high school?"

nam_3.text: *Ploy holds it up by one leg. Jane laughs. Bow laughs.*

nam_4.text: *Nam's face goes very still. Elysia knows that face. She wore it for a whole week in third grade.*

nam_5.text: *Check: Ploy, laughing. Jane, laughing. Bow, laughing. Nam, frozen.*

nam_6.speaker: Elysia
nam_6.text: If I laugh, it's over in a second. If I don't...

nam_laugh_1.text: *She laughs. It's easy. Her body knows how.*

nam_laugh_2.text: *Ploy tosses the frog back. Nam puts it in her pocket instead of back on her bag, and bends over her drawing.*

nam_laugh_3.text: *Elysia feels sick for the rest of the afternoon. She tells herself it's the cafeteria fish.*

nam_cute_2.text: *Check: Ploy, confused. Jane, looking at Ploy. Bow, looking at me.*

nam_cute_5.text: *Elysia gives Nam a small smile, just for her. Nam stares back, surprised. Then she hooks the frog back onto her bag, right where it was.*

pun_1.text: *The fourth week. Pun comes home from school and doesn't go to his jar. He sits at the kitchen table with his backpack still on.*

pun_4.text: *Check: shoulders up. Mouth tight. He's eight. He's terrible at this.*

pun_6.speaker: Pun
pun_6.text: "...They call me slime boy. I took my slime mold for show-and-tell and Tee smeared it all over the inside of my bag. Everyone laughed."

pun_8.speaker: Elysia
pun_8.text: Third grade. Slime in my bag. A whole week.

pun_9.speaker: Elysia
pun_9.text: He's going to go through what I went through. Unless he learns what I learned.

pun_10.text: *She knows exactly what she learned. She could teach it to him in one sentence.*

choices.text: "Maybe... keep the slime at home? Just at school. Just for a while."
"Then be slime boy. Slime boy is the best kind of boy."

pun_hide_1.text: *Pun looks at her for a long time.*

pun_hide_3.text: *He goes to his room. Later, when she walks past, the jar on his windowsill is empty. The lid is off. He took the slime mold back to the drain where he found it.*

pun_hide_4.text: *She stands in the doorway and can't breathe properly.*

pun_hide_5.speaker: Elysia
pun_hide_5.text: I did that. I did what they did to me. I was just nice about it.

pun_bug_2.speaker: Elysia
pun_bug_2.text: "Really. Tee is going to be boring his whole life. You're going to know what a Physarum is."

pun_bug_4.text: *So she tells him. Sitting on his bedroom floor with her nose against the jar, like she's eight too.*

sports_1.text: *Friday. Sports day. Her class team is red, and she's on the cheer squad. She shouts until her voice goes. The version is very good at sports day.*

sports_2.text: *At the water station by the track, Kay is filling paper cups. Alone. Clipboard under his arm. Grey.*

sports_3.text: *Somewhere in the middle of the field, Ulyn is shouting into a megaphone.*

sports_4.text: *She doesn't know Ulyn well. He's funny. Everyone likes him. He's Kay's best friend.*

sports_5.speaker: Elysia
sports_5.text: Kay talks about him like a house he used to live in. Same street. Name still on the mailbox.

sports_6.speaker: Elysia
sports_6.text: I don't know what happened between them. Kay has never said.

choices.text: Get him a cold drink, in front of everyone

sports_drink_1.text: *She buys a cold drink from the canteen, runs over, and pushes it into his hands.*

sports_drink_2.speaker: Elysia
sports_drink_2.real_text: "You looked thirsty. And kind of alone."

sports_drink_3.text: *She sprints away before her friends can catch up, before he can say anything, before she can check anyone's face. Behind her, Ploy yells "ELYSIAAAA" in the voice that means teasing.*

sports_drink_4.text: *She looks back once. Kay is holding the drink with both hands, like it's made of glass.*

sports_stay_1.speaker: Elysia
sports_stay_1.text: He doesn't want people looking at us like that.

sports_stay_2.text: *From across the field, she watches him fill cup after cup. He doesn't drink any.*

mid_1.text: *The fifth week. Midterms. Ploy and her boyfriend break up on Monday.*

mid_2.text: *Ploy calls Monday night. Tuesday night. Wednesday night. Elysia answers every time and listens until two, three, four. She studies chemistry in the gaps.*

mid_3.text: *On Thursday her history score is twelve points lower than usual. Mom sees the paper on the table.*

mid_4.speaker: Mom
mid_4.text: "Elysia. What happened? You're always so good at history."

mid_6.speaker: Mom
mid_6.text: "You're on your phone too much. I see your light on at three in the morning."

choices.text: "Ploy's going through a breakup. She calls me every night. I don't know how to say no."

mid_sorry_1.speaker: Mom
mid_sorry_1.text: "Okay. I know you will. You're my easy one."

mid_sorry_2.text: *Elysia goes upstairs, sits on her bed, and doesn't cry. Easy ones don't.*

mid_honest_3.speaker: Mom
mid_honest_3.text: "Oh, sweetheart. You know you're allowed to hang up, right?"

mid_honest_5.speaker: Mom
mid_honest_5.text: "Maybe. And you're hurt now. Somebody's going to be hurt either way. It doesn't always have to be you."

mid_honest_6.text: *Elysia thinks about that sentence for a long time.*

thu_1.text: *The sixth Thursday. Kay isn't at the gate. She always knows when he's there, and this morning she knows he isn't.*

thu_2.speaker: Elysia
thu_2.text: K? didn't see u at the gate 👀

thu_6.speaker: Elysia
thu_6.text: Kay doesn't get sick. Kay gets sick and comes anyway, grey, and says it's fine.

thu_7.text: *9:41. Math. Her phone buzzes in her pocket.*

thu_10.speaker: Elysia
thu_10.text: Couldn't. Not didn't. Not slept in. Not sick, lol.

thu_12.text: *She knows that word. She's never said it out loud. But she's felt it, some mornings, lying in bed while her body simply refused.*

thu_13.text: *Her thumbs are shaking. "ARE YOU OK." Delete. "what happened." Delete. "i'm calling you." Delete.*

thu_14.speaker: Elysia
thu_14.text: If it were me, what would I want someone to say?

thu_15.speaker: Elysia
thu_15.text: ok. thank u for telling me.

thu_16.speaker: Elysia
thu_16.text: do u want me to call or do u want me to leave u alone

thu_18.speaker: Kay
thu_18.text: leave me alone for now. sorry

thu_19.speaker: Elysia
thu_19.text: Don't be sorry. Don't you dare be sorry.

thu_21.text: *She puts the phone face down on her math book and stares at the board until the numbers stop swimming.*

thu_22.text: *At lunch, she doesn't go to the table by the window.*

thu_23.speaker: Elysia
thu_23.text: He asked me to leave him alone. I want to respect that. But someone should go.

thu_ulyn_1.text: *Ulyn is at the end of a cafeteria table, about to sit down. She's never really talked to him without Kay.*

thu_ulyn_2.speaker: Elysia
thu_ulyn_2.text: "Can I talk to you? Just for a second."

thu_ulyn_3.text: *By the drinks fridge, she tells him. Couldn't. She watches his face go white, then very still, then focused, like a cat.*

thu_ulyn_4.speaker: Elysia
thu_ulyn_4.text: He knows something. Something I don't.

thu_ulyn_5.speaker: Elysia
thu_ulyn_5.text: "He asked me to leave him alone for now. So I am. I want to respect that."

thu_ulyn_6.speaker: Elysia
thu_ulyn_6.text: "But you're... different. You're Ulyn. He talks about you like..."

thu_ulyn_7.text: *She doesn't finish. Like a house he used to live in. Ulyn doesn't need to hear that right now.*

thu_ulyn_8.speaker: Elysia
thu_ulyn_8.text: "Could you go see him? After school?"

thu_ulyn_10.speaker: Elysia
thu_ulyn_10.text: "Don't tell him I asked you. He'll think he's a bother."

thu_go_1.text: *After school she walks to Kay's street. She's been there twice, both times with him.*

thu_go_3.text: *Two people on Kay's front step. Kay, in a T-shirt. Ulyn, still in uniform, a plastic bag between them.*

thu_go_4.text: *Kay's face is wet. Ulyn isn't looking at him. On purpose. The way you don't look at someone when you're letting them cry.*

thu_go_6.speaker: Elysia
thu_go_6.text: He has someone. Right now, he has someone.

thu_go_7.text: *Her chest aches in two directions at once. Good, good, good. And: it wasn't me.*

thu_go_8.text: *She turns around and walks home. She doesn't tell anyone she was there.*

thu_wait_1.text: *She doesn't go. She doesn't ask anyone. She sits through the afternoon and checks her phone every four minutes. Nothing.*

thu_wait_2.speaker: Elysia
thu_wait_2.text: I did the right thing. He asked for space.

thu_wait_3.speaker: Elysia
thu_wait_3.text: Then why does it feel like I did nothing?

thu_night_3.text: *He doesn't reply. It says Read at 9:14.*

thu_ulyn_text_1.text: *7:02 p.m. A number she saved two months ago and never used.*

thu_ulyn_text_2.speaker: Ulyn
thu_ulyn_text_2.text: he's ok. ish. thanks for telling me.

thu_ulyn_text_3.text: *Elysia goes into the bathroom, turns on the fan so Pun won't hear, and cries for twenty minutes.*

fri_1.text: *Friday night, she types for an hour and deletes all of it. Then:*

fri_2.speaker: Elysia
fri_2.text: tomorrow. 10am. i'm picking u up. no is not an option 😤

sat_2.text: *She takes him to the park by the canal and hands him a can of milk tea. A monitor lizard swims past very slowly, like it has somewhere to be.*

sat_3.text: *She thinks about the museum across the river. The back room. The fact that she's never brought anyone.*

sat_museum_1.text: *She takes him to the natural history museum across the river. Free on Saturdays.*

sat_museum_2.text: *Straight past the dinosaurs, to a dim room at the back. Fungi and slime molds: tiny dried specimens in matchbox trays, labeled in tiny old handwriting. An old screen in the corner loops a time-lapse of something yellow solving a maze.*

sat_museum_3.text: *She has come here alone maybe thirty times since third grade.*

sat_museum_4.speaker: Elysia
sat_museum_4.text: "I've never brought anyone here. Not even Mint. Mint knows. But I've never brought anyone."

sat_museum_5.text: *Kay looks around the room like it's a church.*

sat_talk_1.speaker: Elysia
sat_talk_1.text: "You told me you couldn't get up. Thank you for telling me. You don't have to explain it."

sat_talk_2.text: *Kay is quiet for a long moment.*

sat_talk_3.speaker: Kay
sat_talk_3.text: "I want to explain it. Some of it."

sat_talk_4.text: *So he tells her. Not everything. She can tell there are rooms he isn't opening.*

sat_talk_5.text: *The mornings. The weight. Everything feeling far away. Ulyn came over, and they talked about something old.*

sat_talk_6.speaker: Elysia
sat_talk_6.text: Something old. The house on the same street, I think. I might never know.

sat_talk_7.speaker: Kay
sat_talk_7.text: "At school I keep away from you because I think being seen with me makes people talk about you. Makes you look weird."

sat_talk_10.speaker: Elysia
sat_talk_10.text: He wasn't embarrassed of me. He thought he was the embarrassing one.

sat_talk_11.text: *Six weeks of a story. The walk home. Shouldn't. People looking at us like that. Every brick of it was third grade. Every brick was wrong.*

sat_talk_12.speaker: Elysia
sat_talk_12.text: "You think you make me look weird?"

sat_talk_13.text: *She laughs, because it's absurd. Then she stops, because it isn't.*

sat_talk_14.text: *Check: his face. He means it. He really means it.*

choices.text: Tell him the truth. All of it.
"Kay, that's silly! You don't make me look weird at all!"

sat_truth_1.speaker: Elysia
sat_truth_1.text: "K. I used to be the weird kid."

sat_truth_2.text: *She says it to her shoes. It's easier.*

sat_truth_3.speaker: Elysia
sat_truth_3.text: "Slime girl. In third grade a boy scraped slime off a rotten log and smeared it inside my bag, and everyone laughed for a whole week. And I decided I'd never be weird again. Ever."

sat_truth_4.speaker: Elysia
sat_truth_4.text: "I watch everything I say. Every single thing. With my friends I'm doing a version. The fun one. The one who's always fine."

sat_truth_6.speaker: Elysia
sat_truth_6.text: "You and Mint are the only people I don't do the version with. So when you won't walk with me because people will talk, it feels like you're agreeing with them. Like even you think I should be careful."

sat_truth_7.speaker: Kay
sat_truth_7.text: "I didn't— I thought I was protecting you."

sat_truth_9.text: *She leans her head on his shoulder. She can feel him breathing.*

sat_truth_10.speaker: Elysia
sat_truth_10.text: "I said I don't care what they think. I lied too. I care so much it makes me tired. But I care about you more."

sat_truth_12.speaker: Kay
sat_truth_12.text: "You don't have to do the version with me. Ever."

sat_truth_13.text: *She cries a little and laughs at the same time.*

sat_truth_14.speaker: Elysia
sat_truth_14.text: "Okay. Then you don't have to be fine with me. Deal?"

sat_version_1.speaker: Elysia
sat_version_1.text: "Kay, that's silly! You don't make me look weird at all! My friends love you!"

sat_version_4.text: *She feels the moment close like a door she was standing in. He told her something real, and she handed him the version back.*

sat_version_6.text: *She knows why. She's been doing it since she was eight.*

sat_version_10.text: *He is. They sit until the milk tea is warm. Neither of them says anything else real.*

mon_1.text: *Monday. Ploy, Jane, Bow, and Mint, who has drifted over from her own class for reasons she won't explain.*

mon_2.text: *Elysia feels Kay behind her. She turns around and waves.*

mon_3.text: *Kay waves back. Faster than last time. Not as stiff. She waves until he goes inside.*

mon_walk_2.text: *He walks over. Straight across the front of the school, in front of everyone.*

mon_walk_3.text: *Check: Ploy, mouth open. Jane, grabbing Bow's arm. Bow, phone already up.*

choices.text: "Yes, he's my boyfriend, we all know, moving on."

mon_say_1.text: *She takes his hand in front of all of them and doesn't let go.*

mon_say_2.text: *Her face is on fire. Ploy is making a noise like a kettle. From the top of the stairs, someone whoops. Ulyn, she thinks.*

mon_say_3.text: *Mint gives Kay a very small thumbs up.*

mon_say_4.speaker: Elysia
mon_say_4.text: Why is Mint giving Kay a thumbs up?

mon_say_6.text: *Later, in the hallway, Ploy grabs her arm.*

mon_say_8.text: *Check: Ploy. Not mad. Surprised. Maybe a little impressed.*

mon_like_2.text: *Ploy stares. Then she laughs, a real one.*

mon_like_3.speaker: Ploy
mon_like_3.text: "Okay. Okay! Good for you. He's still weird, though."

mon_like_5.text: *Ploy doesn't know what to do with that, so she just links arms with her, and they go to class.*

mon_much_2.speaker: Elysia
mon_much_2.text: Too much. I was too much.

mon_much_3.text: *She puts the feeling back in its box.*

mon_hi_1.text: *She says it in the version voice. Bright. Easy. Kay stops a step away.*

mon_hi_2.text: *Check: his face. It flickers, just like at the canal.*

mon_hi_4.text: *He stands next to her friends for a minute. Then he goes to class.*

late_1.text: *The eighth week. Ploy has a new crush, and the new crush has started leaving her on read.*

late_2.text: *1:12 a.m. Elysia's phone lights up the ceiling. Ploy.*

late_3.text: *She watches it ring. She thinks about Mom. It doesn't always have to be you. She thinks about Kay saying "couldn't."*

choices.text: Answer, and say it. "I can't do 1 a.m. calls anymore."

late_no_1.speaker: Elysia
late_no_1.text: "Ploy, I love you. But I can't do 1 a.m. calls anymore. Lunch tomorrow?"

late_no_3.speaker: Ploy
late_no_3.text: "...Oh. Okay. Yeah. Sorry for bothering you."

late_no_4.speaker: Elysia
late_no_4.text: "You're not bothering me. I just need to sleep. Lunch. I promise."

late_no_6.text: *Ploy is cold for two days. She sits with Jane on Tuesday. She doesn't laugh at Elysia's jokes on Wednesday.*

late_no_7.text: *Check: Ploy, cold. Jane, awkward. Bow, doesn't know which side to be on.*

late_no_8.text: *On Thursday, Ploy sits down across from her at lunch and stabs her rice.*

late_no_9.speaker: Ploy
late_no_9.text: "You could've said that earlier. Like, months ago."

late_no_11.speaker: Ploy
late_no_11.text: "I didn't know it was that much. ...Sorry."

late_no_13.text: *She stops. Then she says the true thing.*

late_no_14.speaker: Elysia
late_no_14.text: "It wasn't okay. But it's okay now."

late_yes_1.text: *She listens until three. Ploy feels better.*

late_yes_2.text: *Elysia lies awake until five and goes to school with stinging eyes.*

art_1.text: *In art class that week, Elysia sits next to Nam.*

art_2.text: *Nam glances up, wary, then back at her paper.*

art_3.speaker: Elysia
art_3.text: "I'm sorry. About the frog. I laughed. I shouldn't have."

art_4.text: *Nam looks at her for a long time. Then she takes the frog out of her pocket and hooks it back onto her bag.*

art_5.text: *The next week, a tiny slime mold appears in yellow pen in the margin of Elysia's worksheet.*

art_beetle_1.text: *Nam smiles when she sits down. Without saying anything, she draws a tiny slime mold in the margin of Elysia's worksheet. Yellow pen, branching like a map. Perfect.*

note_1.text: *The ninth week. Kay's group presents the garden project.*

note_2.text: *Mint heard from someone in Kay's class that Bank answered a question by himself, and Kay just stood there smiling, "which was weird for him."*

note_4.text: *For the first time, the word sounds nice.*

note_5.text: *That night she digs a box out of the back of her closet. Under old birthday cards and a broken Tamagotchi: a notebook from third grade. Stickers on the cover. A slime mold on every page, in careful yellow crayon, the Latin name copied underneath in big wobbly letters. A dried oat flake still taped inside the cover.*

note_7.text: *His windowsill is still empty. It has been for five weeks.*

note_8.speaker: Elysia
note_8.text: "Pun. I was wrong. About keeping the slime at home. I was wrong."

note_10.speaker: Elysia
note_10.text: "When I was your age, someone put slime in my bag too. And I stopped liking things out loud. And I thought that was me being smart."

note_11.speaker: Elysia
note_11.text: "It wasn't smart. It was just sad. Be slime boy. Slime boy is the best kind of boy."

note_12.text: *Pun opens the notebook. He turns the pages slowly, then faster.*

choices.text: "And if anyone says it's weird, tell them your sister said so too."
Just leave the notebook and go

note_hide_yes_1.text: *Pun grins so wide she can see the gap where his tooth fell out.*

note_hide_yes_2.text: *The next morning, there's a slime mold in the jar on the windowsill again.*

note_hide_no_1.text: *She puts it on his desk and goes. Through the wall, she hears him turning the pages for an hour.*

note_hide_no_2.text: *The next morning, there's a slime mold in the jar on the windowsill again.*

note_bug_1.text: *Pun's windowsill has three jars now. Slime boy for five weeks, and he's decided he likes it. Two other kids in his class have started growing their own.*

note_bug_2.speaker: Elysia
note_bug_2.text: "Look. I made this when I was your age."

note_bug_yes_1.text: *Pun looks at her like she just admitted to being a superhero.*

note_bug_no_2.text: *She doesn't know what to do with the word "were."*

last_1.text: *Friday. The last day of the semester.*

last_2.text: *Last night, Pun found a slime mold on the drain cover. Huge. Yellow and foamy, like someone dropped scrambled eggs. It's called dog vomit slime mold, which Pun thinks is the best name anything has ever had. He let her take a picture before he named it Kay. She didn't explain why that was funny.*

last_3.text: *At the gate: Ploy, Jane, Bow, Mint. Elysia has the picture on her phone.*

choices.text: Hold it up for everyone. Don't check.
Show it just to Kay, quietly

last_all_2.text: *Ploy makes a face. Jane says "ew," fondly. Bow takes a screenshot.*

last_all_3.text: *Elysia doesn't look over her shoulder. She doesn't check anyone's face.*

last_all_4.text: *She notices, a second later, that she didn't check. The way you notice a headache is gone.*

last_kay_1.text: *She waits until Kay is next to her, then tilts her phone so only he can see.*

mint_1.text: *At lunch, Mint sits down across from her with a carton of chocolate milk and her about-to-confess face.*

mint_2.speaker: Mint
mint_2.text: "Kay's good for you. I wasn't sure at first."

mint_4.speaker: Mint
mint_4.text: "He looked like someone who'd say 'it's fine' about a broken leg. Guess you're the same, though."

mint_confess_1.speaker: Mint
mint_confess_1.text: "So. In the second week, I sort of talked to Kay."

mint_confess_3.speaker: Mint
mint_confess_3.text: "Outside the library. I told him you'd been tired lately, and you'd rather explode than be a bother to anyone. And to look out for you."

mint_confess_4.speaker: Mint
mint_confess_4.text: "I also told him you two were the same kind of idiot."

mint_confess_7.text: *Elysia opens her mouth. Closes it. She thinks about the back room, and the canal, and "couldn't."*

endA_1.text: *On Sunday, she takes Pun to the natural history museum across the river.*

endA_2.text: *Straight past the dinosaurs to the dim room at the back. Pun presses his nose to the first case and fogs it up completely.*

endA_3.speaker: Pun
endA_3.text: "Physarum. Elysia. ELYSIA. That's the one from your notebook!"

endA_kay_1.text: *Kay is there too, a few steps behind, looking at the cases the way she looks at them. Pun has already decided Kay is his best friend, mostly because of the slime mold's name.*

endA_ploy_2.text: *She ignores it. Today it can wait.*

endA_pics_1.speaker: Ploy
endA_pics_1.text: send me a pic of the slime. i want to see what the big deal is

endA_pics_3.speaker: Ploy
endA_pics_3.text: ok that one is actually kind of cool

endA_end_1.text: *They stay until closing. She tells Pun everything. The oat flakes. The train lines. The maze it remembers.*

endA_end_2.text: *She talks loud and fast, the slime girl way, and doesn't check anyone's face once.*

endA_end_3.text: *On the bus home, Pun falls asleep against her shoulder, holding her notebook.*

endA_end_5.text: *She tests it. It doesn't hurt. It feels like taking off shoes that were too small.*

endB_1.text: *She still does the version sometimes. At the gate. When Ploy is having a bad day. It's easier than not.*

endB_2.text: *But not all the time. Not with Kay. Not with Mint. Some days, not with Pun.*

endB_3.text: *That night, Ploy calls at 12:40. Elysia answers.*

endB_4.speaker: Elysia
endB_4.text: "Hey. Can I call you back tomorrow? I'm really tired."

endB_6.text: *It's not a big speech. It's one sentence. She lies in bed afterward, heart pounding, like she ran somewhere.*

endB_9.speaker: Elysia
endB_9.text: i said no to ploy. kind of.

endB_13.text: *He does know. She can tell. That's the thing about Kay.*

endC_1.text: *Everyone says Elysia is "so easy to be around." Ploy says it. Mom says it. Her report card says "a pleasure to have in class."*

endC_2.text: *That night, Ploy calls at 1:04 a.m. Elysia answers. She listens until three.*

endC_3.text: *Afterward she lies in the dark. Somewhere in the house, Pun is asleep next to his windowsill.*

endC_msg_2.text: *She looks at the smiley face. She knows that smiley face. She's been wearing it since third grade.*

endC_msg_6.text: *The message sits there. The cursor blinks. It's still hers to send.*
